obr_outturn._comment: The emulator and EFO columns stay the November 2025 EFO study in papers/obr-macro/figures/fig_outturn_data.csv. Only the ONS outturn is refreshed, from one pinned file in the append-only vintage store, so a later ONS revision cannot move the chart silently: re-pin here to rescore. The working paper scored against the 14 May 2026 first quarterly estimate (0.1, 0.2, 0.2, 0.6), which is still the ons_outturn_qoq_pct column of that CSV.
obr_outturn.source: ONS ABMI (GDP, chained volume measure, seasonally adjusted), release_updated 2026-11-12, fetched 2026-11-16; quarter-on-quarter growth computed from the levels

obr_computed_share.source: docs/calibration_scorecard.md in the PolicyEngine/obr-macroeconomic-model repository at commit 0e44ec8 (October 2026 EFO; default nominal-GDP-pin closure; CI run 44392267520). At 0e44ec8 the forecast 16+ population follows the EFO-implied path (PR #74), which moved the unemployment rate 1.17pp to 0.62pp (poor to fair), real GDP 4.05 to 4.24, consumption 6.92 to 7.23, household income 3.08 to 3.10, real household income 3.29 to 3.30 and company profits 11.66 to 12.88; GDP and consumption read worse because the drained unemployment had been lifting raw consumption, an artefact of the frozen population, not fit. Earlier, household taxes TYWHH were held on their data path (PR #71, at 0fe04c9). Before that, the March 2026 vintage under the published closure, before the receipts identities (#56) and the ended EU payments (#62)
obr_computed_share.bands_note: bands: rates ±1.0pp · net balances ±1.5% of GDP · levels ≤10% MAPE
obr_computed_share._grades_comment: The 11 computed variables graded against the bands above. 'identity' is employment, where both inputs are themselves passthrough, so the accounting identity closes trivially and the pass carries no information.

frbus_residuals.source: us-frb-model VALIDATION.md at 162cfe6 (October 2026 LONGBASE, rerun 16 Nov 2026): Test 1 tracking table and the pyfrbus 1.1.1 cross-check table. The paper (papers/frb-us/sections/validation.tex) reports the April 2026 vintage
frbus_residuals._series_comment: series is the row's KIND of comparison, not a decoration: 1 = ours against the Fed's implementation under shock (the evidence), 2 = the Fed's own two releases against each other (the reference-noise yardstick our rows are judged against), 3 = a tracking identity that re-solves to its own input and therefore cannot fail. Series 3 was previously 1 on the first row, which painted the row the page calls 'not evidence' in the accent colour.

rows.label: ours vs LONGBASE — tracking identity, not evidence
rows.note: init_trac defines add-factors as minus the residuals at the input data, so re-solving reproduces it up to float64 for ANY input — verified: the same test passes at 9.0e-9 on randomly scrambled data. Shown for completeness; it measures arithmetic, not economics.

rows.label: pyfrbus 1.1.1 vs 1.0.0 — the Fed’s own releases

define_emissions._comment: What the define-uk divergence gate actually pins is the RATIO of the pinned run to the manual's Table 4, not the two levels: the levels in validation/figures/data/define_emissions_divergence.csv are rounded to whole MtCO2e, so recomputing the percentage from them gives -3.4 / -10.2 / -23.1 where the gate and the validation page say -3.5 / -10.2 / -23.3. The bars plot the rounded levels; the percentages come from the gated ratios below.
define_emissions.source: validation/reference_outputs.json in the PolicyEngine define-uk adapter repository (the divergence gate, pinned to ±0.02), as recorded in that repository's VALIDATION.md target 1b and published on define/validation/
